gospelTitle: Signs of the End, and a Warning Against Deception

retelling.text: Some people admire the Temple, noting its beautiful stones and the gifts offered there. Jesus tells them that the day is coming when every stone will be torn down and not one will be left standing on another.
His listeners want to know more and ask when this will happen. They also want to know what sign will show that it is about to take place.
Jesus warns them not to be led astray. Many will claim to speak in His name, saying that they are the one or that the time has come, and His followers must not go after them.
When they hear of wars and uprisings, they should not be overcome by fear. These things must happen first, but they do not mean the end has arrived.
Jesus continues that nations and kingdoms will fight one another. There will be great earthquakes, hunger and disease in many places, along with frightening sights and signs in the heavens.

reflectionTitle: Tuesday of the Thirty-Fourth Week: Standing Firm When Everything Shifts
reflection: As the Church year draws to a close, our readings turn toward the end of all things. Today we also honor Saint Andrew Dung-Lac and his companions, who stayed faithful even to death.
In the First Reading, John sees a harvest. The Son of Man and His angels gather what is ripe, and nothing escapes God's notice or His justice.
The Psalm answers with trust rather than fear. The Lord is King, He governs with fairness, and even the sea and the forests rejoice at His coming.
In the Gospel, people admire the beauty of the Temple. Jesus gently reminds them that even the finest things made by human hands will not last.
Then He gives a surprising instruction. When the world is loud with wars, disasters and rumors, we are not to be terrified.
He also warns about something quieter than disaster: deception. Many voices will say that they have the answer, and some will even use His name.
That is a challenge for us. Fear makes us hungry for easy answers, and anyone who sounds confident can seem trustworthy.
The martyrs show us another way. They held on to Christ when it cost them everything, because their hope was in Him and not in anything that could be taken away.
In daily life, we feel small versions of these shaking times. A job changes, a family faces illness, or the news makes everything feel uncertain.
At work, a leader sets the tone. If you stay calm, listen well and speak honestly, your team can borrow some of your steadiness.
Be careful, too, about chasing every new trend or loud opinion. Ask whether it is true, whether it is just, and whether it leads people toward Christ.
At home, we can build what lasts: patience, forgiveness, prayer at the table, and time given freely to those we love.
In our communities, we can serve quietly, knowing that the kindness we offer now is part of what God will gather in the end.
Today, take a moment to name one thing that worries you. Hand it to the Lord, and then do the next good thing in front of you.
message: When the world feels unsteady, do not be afraid or deceived; stay close to Christ, who alone is lasting, and keep doing good with a calm heart.
